name: Ralte
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Grierson, G. A. (1904) Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Pt. III, Ralte sketch (Kuki-Chin group); scanned volume not scannable for a stress statement online

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2021. ラルテー語の音韻とクキ・チン祖語 [A phonological comparison of Ralte and Proto-Kuki-Chin]. ありあけ 熊本大学言語学論集 (ARIAKE Kumamoto University Linguistic Papers) 20: 21-38.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Revised phonology (sec. 2, pp. 22-25): syllable (C1)V(C2)(C3)/T, three tones (low level, rising, falling) plus a possible 4th pitch pattern on glottal/short checked syllables; sec. 2.3 p. 24: long vowels/diphthongs shorten in the first syllable of compounds and derived words and that syllable surfaces with low level tone. No 強勢/ストレス/アクセント anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2019. ラルテー語における動詞語幹の交替 [Verb stem alternation in Ralte]. 言語文化研究 (Graduate School of Language and Culture, Osaka University) 45: 161-178. hdl:11094/71637
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6 音韻 (pp. 164-165): syllable (C1)V(C2)(C3)/T, consonants, vowels, 2.6.4 three tonemes (rising, low level, falling); short open syllables all low level; checked syllables low pitch / high after low. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2017. ラルテー語における再帰・相互標識 -duːn˩˥ [The reflexive/reciprocal marker -duːn in Ralte]. 東京大学言語学論集 (TULIP) 38: 233-245.
sources.note: Nothing. Scanned; sec. 2 音韻 pp. 234-235: syllable, consonants, vowels, 2.4 three tones + tone sandhi. No stress.

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2016. ラルテー語の人称標示 [Person marking in Ralte]. 東京大学言語学論集 (eTULIP) 37: e19-e28.
sources.note: Nothing. Scanned; p. e19 sec. 2 one-paragraph phonology: inventory, three tonemes (rising, mid level, falling), checked syllables low pitch. No stress.
sources.venue: 東京大学言語学論集 (eTULIP) 37: e19-e28

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2016. ラルテー語の基礎語彙とテキスト [A basic vocabulary and a text of the Ralte language]. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics (AALL) 10: 325-344.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 音韻 (pp. 328-329): consonants, vowels with length, three tones (low level, rising, falling) and checked-syllable sandhi; no stress statement.
sources.venue: Asian and African Languages and Linguistics (AALL)

sources.citation: Otsuka, Kosei 2015. ラルテー語における音韻体系: ミゾ語およびティディム・チン語との対照的考察 [The phonological system of the Ralte language: a comparative study of Ralte, Mizo, and Tiddim Chin]. 東京大学言語学論集 (TULIP) 36: e49-e59.
sources.note: Nothing. Body is a scanned image (read visually, all 11 pp.). Sec. 2.1 syllable C1(V1)V2(V3)(C2)/T; 2.2 consonants; 2.3 vowels i e a o u with length contrast; 2.4 tone: three tonemes (rising LH, low level LL, falling HL), checked syllables low pitch (high after low-level tone). No mention of stress/accent (強勢/アクセント).
sources.venue: 東京大学言語学論集 (TULIP) 36: e49-e59

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Ralte' pp. 75-78 (+ specimen).
sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. 'Pronunciation' paragraph (p. 75-76) only discusses vowel length ('probably every final vowel of a word or syllable is long, just as in Lushei'), h for abrupt shortening, euphonic v/m, ch ~ Lushei f; based solely on a Prodigal Son specimen.
sources.venue: III Tibeto-Burman Family, Part III Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups

sources.citation: 大塚行誠 (Otsuka, Kosei). 2017. 科学研究費助成事業 研究成果報告書『インド北東部におけるラルテー語の記述言語学的な研究』[Grants-in-Aid final research report: Descriptive Studies of the Ralte language in Northeast India], KAKENHI project 26770136 (Young Scientists (B), 2014-2016), Tokyo University of Foreign Studies / ILCAA. 4 pp. (dated 2017-06-16).
sources.note: No tone inventory is stated: sec. 4(1) says only that Ralte 'syllable structure and phonemes' were reported (in Otsuka 2015) in contrast with Mizo and Tiddim Chin; tone appears only as a tone letter on the derived reflexive/reciprocal form -dut˩ (sec. 4(5)). Also announces a grammar sketch and text collection 'in preparation for public release' and recordings (folk tale Chemtatrawta, songs, conversation) being transcribed for archiving - pointers to future tone-bearing materials.
